transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because at work, when I’m trying to explain things—like the inventory numbers, or who’s supposed to be on the weekend schedule—it just kind of… jumps around. I’ll start with the truck delivery, then I’m talking about Thursday, and then I’m remembering the church grill, and then my boss’s tone of voice, like the way he said it, and people just stare at me like they don’t know how I got there.

I mean, I know what I’m trying to say, mostly, but it doesn’t come out straight. It’s been causing problems.
Does this jumping around in your speech happen only at work or does it also happen in other areas of your life?

It’s mostly work that I notice it, because that’s where people stop me, you know? Like I’ll be trying to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then I’m on about the trucks, and Thursday, and the church grill, and my boss’s tone—like the way he said something—and then everybody’s looking at me like they lost the thread.

I guess it probably happens other places too, but work is where it gets pointed out.
Have you always had this kind of trouble with your speech, or is it something that started more recently?

I don’t think it was always like this. I mean, I’ve always maybe talked a little too much, my wife used to say I’d take the scenic route to answer a simple thing, like when we’d be driving and I’d point out the old hardware store that isn’t even there anymore… but this jumbled-up thing, where I stop weird on the sales floor or can’t keep the explanation in order, that’s more recent.

I’d say people really started noticing it about six months ago. Maybe around then.
Do you have trouble remembering things or learning new information at work or in your daily life?

I don’t know… I mean, remembering, like, where I put my keys? Everybody does that. At work I use the clipboard and the little sticky notes, and sometimes I’ll walk to the back room and think, wait, was I getting price tags or did Jerry ask about the endcap—Jerry’s got this way of leaving the box cutter on the soda shelf, which drives me crazy—

But learning new stuff… I don’t think that’s the main thing. If someone shows me the scanner update, I can usually get it. It’s more like… I start explaining it and then I’m somewhere else. So I’m not sure if that’s memory or just me getting turned around while I’m talking.
Do you have trouble writing things down, like notes or emails, in a way that makes sense to others?

Yeah… with notes too, sometimes. Like if I’m trying to write down the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it’ll start out normal, and then I’ll add something about the trucks coming in, or Thursday, or—there’s this church grill thing I was supposed to remember—and then I’m thinking about my boss’s tone when he asked me, and by the time someone reads it they’re like, “What does this mean?”

It’s not that I don’t know what I meant when I started. It just kind of… jumps around on me.
Do you find that your writing, like notes or emails, usually makes sense to others, or is it also often confusing like your spoken explanations?

It’s often confusing, yeah. Not always, but enough that people will ask me what I meant. I’ll be writing something simple, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then it starts turning into trucks coming in, and Thursday, and that church grill I was supposed to remember, and then I’m thinking about my boss’s tone when he asked me about it.

So by the time somebody reads it, it doesn’t really line up. It’s kind of like when I’m talking—my words just jump around, and people look at me like they can’t follow where I went.
Do you have trouble following conversations when other people are talking?

Sometimes, yeah… I mean, if it’s just one person and they say it straight, I can usually follow. But if people are talking over each other, like at the store when the front register is beeping and someone’s asking about coupons and then Jerry starts telling me about the delivery—then I kind of lose the thread.

But I don’t know if that’s the conversation or just… there’s too much happening. I’ll catch one part, like “endcap,” and then I’m thinking about which aisle that was, and then they’ve moved on. So I might ask them to say it again, or I just nod, which I probably shouldn’t do.
Do you have trouble with tasks that require planning or organizing, outside of just explaining things or writing notes?

Yeah… planning stuff gets hard, especially on the sales floor. Like I’ll have the schedule clipboard in my hand, and the associates are kind of waiting for me to tell them who goes where, and I’m just… standing there.

Or I’ll walk the same aisle a few times, straightening the batteries again and again, like that’s the thing I’m supposed to be doing, even though there’s other stuff. The batteries always get messed up anyway, people grab the wrong pack, and then the tags—sorry. But yeah, I get stuck doing the same little thing instead of organizing the whole shift.
Do you have trouble making decisions, even about small, everyday things?

I don’t know… I mean, small decisions, like what to eat or which shirt, I guess I don’t think of those as decisions exactly. I just do whatever’s there.

At work, though, sometimes if there’s two things in front of me, I’ll sort of stand there too long. But then again, that could be because the tags are wrong or somebody put seasonal stuff where it doesn’t belong, and then you’re thinking, well, if I move this now, later the truck comes and there’s nowhere for it. They used to send the truck on Wednesdays, then it was Thursdays for a while, and that messed everybody up.

So… I’m not sure if it’s decisions or just everything gets tangled up. I do get stuck sometimes.
Do you have trouble understanding what others are saying to you, or following their instructions?

I’m not sure. I mean, if someone tells me, “Put this on aisle five,” I understand the words. It’s not like they’re speaking another language.

But if they give me three things at once, like “check the cooler, then call back so-and-so, and after that move the display,” I can lose part of it. Then I’m thinking about the cooler because last week the door wasn’t sealing right, and the dairy guy kept saying it was fine, but you could feel it, you know, the cold air coming out.

So… maybe instructions, yeah, if there’s too much packed in there. But simple stuff, I think I understand okay.
Do you often find yourself needing others to repeat what they've said because you didn't understand it the first time?

I’m not sure it’s that I don’t understand it the first time. Sometimes I hear it, but then I’m already thinking about the next thing, or the person is walking away and talking over their shoulder, which people do on the floor all the time.

I might say, “What was that again?” but it’s not always because the words didn’t make sense. It’s more like… I want to make sure I got the right part. Like if they say something about register coverage and then mention returns, I’ll catch one and not the other. But if someone says it plain, I usually get it.
Do you have trouble with word-finding, like thinking of the right word when you're talking?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s not always just one word missing, though. I’ll start trying to explain, like, the inventory numbers or who’s supposed to be on the weekend schedule, and then the words kind of… jump around.

I’ll be talking about the truck, and then Thursdays, because they changed the delivery once, and then I’m thinking about the church grill thing they had out front, and then my boss’s tone when he asked me about it. And I can tell people are looking at me like they’re waiting for the point, like they can’t follow where I’m going.

So maybe it is word-finding, but it feels more like the words don’t stay in the right order.
Do you often have trouble understanding what people are saying to you, even when they speak clearly and slowly?

I don’t know if I’d say often. If someone is speaking clearly and slowly, I usually can follow the words. It’s more when there’s a lot around it, or I start thinking about what they meant by it.

Like at work, somebody can say something simple, and then I’m thinking about whether they’re upset, because the way they stood there reminds me of this old assistant manager we had who used to do that with his keys, jingling them, and then I’m not really on the sentence anymore.

But if you mean the actual words… no, I don’t think I’m usually confused when people say it plainly.
Do you have trouble with tasks that require attention and focus, such as reading or watching TV, outside of work?

Outside of work… I’m not sure. I don’t read much in one sitting anymore, but I don’t know if that’s attention or just, you know, I pick something up and then remember I was going to rinse a dish, and then there’s mail on the counter.

TV is funny because I’ll have it on, but I’m also looking at my phone, or I get up during the commercials even though now you can pause everything. My brother, he watches those old detective shows where you have to catch the clue early, and I always miss who the cousin was or why they went to the cabin. But sometimes the plots are just written badly, honestly.

So… I guess I haven’t really kept track of it. It’s not something I’ve thought about as a problem outside work, exactly.
Do you think it's harder for you to express your thoughts in words or to understand what others are saying to you?

It’s more expressing it, I think. Like I can hear what someone says, most of the time, but when I try to explain something back, that’s when it gets… tangled.

That’s kind of why I came in. At work I’ll try to go over the inventory numbers, or the weekend schedule, and then I’m talking about the truck, and then Thursdays, because the delivery got changed once, and then I remember the church grill they had set up out front, and then I’m thinking about my boss’s tone when he asked me.

And people look at me like they’re waiting for the actual answer. Like they can’t follow what I’m saying. So yeah… I guess putting my thoughts into words is harder.
Do you think your trouble with explaining things is more because you can't find the right words or because you have trouble keeping your thoughts in order?

I think it’s more keeping the thoughts in order. I mean, I know the words, usually. It’s not like I’m standing there trying to remember the word “truck” or “schedule.”

It’s more like I start explaining the inventory numbers, and then I’m on the weekend schedule, and then the truck delivery comes into it, and Thursdays, because that got changed one time, and then I’m remembering that church grill they had set up out front, and then my boss’s tone when he asked me about it… and by then people are looking at me like they don’t know where I’m going with it.

So, yeah. The words are there. They just don’t stay lined up right.
Do you think your trouble with explaining things is related to how you think about the information before you try to say it, or is it more about the act of speaking itself?

I think it’s before I say it… mostly. Like the speaking part works, my mouth works, but what I’m trying to say is already kind of scattered.

That’s why I came in, really. I’ll try to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and then it jumps to the truck, and then Thursday because that’s when something changed once, and then I’m thinking about that church grill they had out front—my boss made a comment about the smoke getting near the doors—and then I’m remembering his tone instead of the actual numbers.

So by the time I’m talking, people are looking at me like they can’t follow it. I don’t blame them exactly. It’s just… I don’t always have it in the right order before it comes out.
Do you think your trouble with explaining things is something that you've always had, even as a child, or is it something that started later in life?

No, not as a kid. I mean, I wasn’t perfect or anything, but I got through school, college, work stuff… I could explain things well enough.

This has been more recent. Maybe… about 11 months? Around when the new district manager started pushing harder on the forecasts and schedules. That’s when it started feeling like my thoughts wouldn’t stay in a straight line. And the forecasts, they changed the forms too, or at least the way he wanted them done, and everyone acted like it was simple, but then the schedule connects to payroll, and the truck times, and then people ask why Saturday is short-staffed—

But, yeah. Not childhood. It started later, about 11 months ago.
Do you think your words get jumbled because you're having trouble thinking of the right words to use, or because you're having trouble organizing your thoughts before you speak?

It’s more the organizing part, I think. The words are there, mostly. I came in because when I try to explain something simple, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts going sideways.

I’ll start with the numbers, then I’m talking about the truck delivery, then Thursday because that’s when it changed once, and then that church grill out front—there was smoke by the doors—and then I’m thinking about my boss’s tone when he said something, not what I was supposed to be explaining.

So it’s not like I can’t think of words. It’s like they don’t come out in the order people expect, and then they look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you think your trouble with explaining things is more related to the words themselves or how you're thinking about what you want to say?

It’s more how I’m thinking it through, I guess. The words themselves are usually there, but they don’t line up right.

Like at work, if I’m trying to explain the inventory numbers or who’s on the weekend schedule, it starts one place and then jumps. I’ll be talking about the trucks, then Thursday because something changed that day, then that church grill outside with the smoke near the doors, and then I’m stuck on how my boss sounded when he said something. And by then the person is just looking at me like… they don’t know where I’m going.

So it’s not exactly the words. It’s the way they get connected before I say them.
